scope: User-requested richer canopy on Habit Oak only; other landmarks and runtime performance excluded.
method: Approved reference and prior beauty viewed first; new rear/profile/beauty/clay inspected individually. Remaining13frames inspected in labelled600x450-per-frame contact sheet. Total17newviews.

findings.richness: Deeper green tones and light/dark differences between overlapping clusters make the beauty image materially richer than v2. Added small leaf shapes break up the smooth outer contour.
findings.attachment: The rear and side clay views preserve substantial branch connections. No detached canopy mass, disappearing rear face or missing major support was observed across the nine-angle orbit.
findings.readability: Main trunk, roots, lower galleries, entrance and twin stairs remain readable. Front-right foliage still partially screens upper treehouse detail, broadly consistent with the previous composition rather than a new identity loss.
findings.identity: The same broad Oak/treehouse silhouette, supporting trunk and surrounding galleries remain recognizable; no visible architectural rearrangement is introduced by the canopy.

residuals.finding: Large rounded flattened clusters still dominate. The improvement is strongest in green palette and modest surface breakup; it does not reproduce the reference's dense fine-leaf canopy.
Several new leaf accents read as small pointed shards on top of the clay clusters rather than coherent leafy sprays. Visible branch-colored patches still meet the canopy surface in the beauty view.

limits: Completed stills do not verify stage-dependent canopy reveal, animation, phone frame rate or runtime batching behavior.
Contact-sheet review establishes broad cross-view consistency, not subpixel geometry or material correctness.
No geometry, runtime source or public asset was edited by the reviewer; only report and temporary analysis contact sheet were written.
